item.title: [−1] Rupee opens 10 paise stronger at 96.22 per dollar as oil eases; October range seen at 95.30–96.80
item.description:
The rupee opened firmer on Monday as crude fell and Fed hike fears eased. A report sees it trading 95.30–96.80 this month, with record forex reserves of $785.71 billion offsetting FPI outflows. Easing after weeks of pressure.

IT services: mild headwind (−1) — Exporters' rupee gains trimmed

Why it matters: A steadier rupee trims imported inflation and the cost of crude, and reduces currency losses that deter foreign investors, while slightly reducing exporters' rupee gains.

Market gauges: Rupee +1, Inflation outlook +1

Confidence: medium · horizon: days

item.title: [−1] Indian IT majors head into results week expecting their weakest September quarter in three years
item.description:
Large IT services firms are expected to report muted revenue growth with stable margins as clients keep discretionary budgets tight. A global IT bellwether raised its FY27 outlook to 3–6% growth but saw no change in demand. Earnings season starts this week.

IT services: mild headwind (−1) — Weakest September quarter in three years

Why it matters: Weak growth at index-heavy IT firms limits earnings support for Indian equities, though AI projects and a weak rupee cushion margins.

Market gauges: Equities (Nifty & Sensex) −1

Confidence: medium · horizon: weeks
